query: For the paper "Automatic Argumentative-Zoning Using Word2vec" (arXiv: 1703.10152), answer this question: What is argumentative zoning?

drafts: Argumentative zoning (AZ), also called rhetorical sentence classification, is a process of assigning rhetorical status to extracted sentences [1]. In this paper, AZ is described as an important task in scientific paper analysis [7], and an example annotation scheme assigns seven categories of rhetorical status to full sentences: aim, contrast, own, background, other, basis and textual [3].

citations.quote: Rhetorical sentence classiﬁcation, also known as argumentative zoning (AZ) [4], is a process of assigning rhetorical status to the extracted sentences.
In comparison with document summarization on the arti- cles from social media and newswire, argumentative zoning (AZ) is an important task in scientiﬁc paper analysis.

Their scheme resulted seven categories of rhetorical status and the categories are assigned to full sentences. Examples 1 of human annotated sentences with their rhetorical status are shown in Table. 1. The seven categories are aim, contrast, own, background, other, basis and textual.

Rhetorical sentence classiﬁcation, also known as argumentative zoning (AZ) [4], is a process of assigning rhetorical status to the extracted sentences.

[3] introduced their rhetorical annotation scheme which takes into account of the aspects of argumentation, metadiscourse and relatedness to other works. Their scheme resulted seven categories of rhetorical status and the categories are assigned to full sentences. Examples 1 of human annotated sentences with their rhetorical status are shown in Table. 1. The seven categories are aim, contrast, own, background, other, basis and textual.
